advisor.summary: The 2019 tri-agency final rule created the Individual Coverage HRA: an employer of any size reimburses individual-market premiums and out-of-pocket medical care, tax-free to employees and deductible to the business, with no statutory dollar cap. ACA integration is solved by requiring every participant to be enrolled in individual-market coverage or Medicare. Benefits may vary across the regulation's defined employee classes but must be uniform within a class, and no class may be offered a choice between the ICHRA and a traditional group plan. As with all §105/§106 arrangements, >2% S corporation shareholders, partners, and sole proprietors cannot participate tax-free — C-corp owner-employees can. The engine models the employer's deduction for reimbursements; employee-side exclusion value and premium-tax-credit displacement are evaluated off-model.
mechanics: The employer sets a fixed monthly allowance per class; employees substantiate individual-market enrollment and expenses; reimbursements are excluded under §106(a) and §105(b) and deducted under §162(a).

Classes must come from the permitted list in Reg. §54.9802-4 — full-time, part-time, salaried, hourly, seasonal, geographic rating area, and others — with same-terms treatment inside each class, varied only by age (up to 3:1) and family size.
An affordable ICHRA offer ends the employee's §36B premium tax credit; the offer must include an annual opt-out so an employee facing an unaffordable allowance can preserve the credit.

For applicable large employers, an affordable ICHRA satisfies the §4980H employer-mandate offer; an unaffordable one exposes the employer to §4980H(b) assessments as employees decline and claim credits.
Minimum class sizes apply to certain classes when a traditional group plan is offered to another class — the regulation's guardrail against shifting risk to the exchanges.

Owner mapping: C-corp owner-employees participate tax-free; §1372 keeps >2% S corporation shareholders (and self-employed owners generally) out — their route is §162(l), and only the entity's deduction for reimbursements is in the model.

authority.note: The ICHRA regulation: permitted classes, same-terms rule, individual-coverage enrollment requirement, and the opt-out right (2019 tri-agency final rule).
Exclude the reimbursements and the coverage itself from employee income.
The employer's deduction for reimbursements — the quantity the engine models.
Premium tax credit coordination: an affordable ICHRA offer bars the credit; an unaffordable one permits opt-out and a PTC claim.
The employer mandate an affordable ICHRA can satisfy for applicable large employers.
Excludes >2% S corporation shareholders from tax-free participation via partner treatment.

requirements: Every participant (and covered dependents) enrolled in individual-market coverage or Medicare, substantiated at enrollment and again with each reimbursement.
A written plan with classes drawn only from the regulation's permitted list and same-terms allowances within each class.
No class offered both the ICHRA and a traditional group plan.
The 90-day advance annual notice covering premium-tax-credit interaction and the opt-out right.
Minimum class sizes respected where a group plan remains for another class.
risks: Substantiation is the leading failure: reimbursing employees who dropped their individual coverage makes the payments taxable and threatens group-health-plan status with §4980D exposure at $100 per employee per day — Reg. §54.9802-4 and Notice 2018-88 frame the compliance boundary.
Improvised classes or minimum-class-size violations void the design's protection.
For applicable large employers, an unaffordable allowance converts into §4980H(b) assessments as employees decline and take the premium tax credit.
For heavily subsidized workforces, an affordable ICHRA can be worth less to employees than the credits they give up — model the workforce before replacing group coverage.
Owner-side expectations: no tax-free self-reimbursement for pass-through owners; the modeled number is the entity deduction only.
stateNotes: Conformity: states conforming to federal income definitions exclude the reimbursements from employee income exactly as federal law does, and the employer deduction follows the ordinary business-income computation.
PTET: for pass-through sponsors the reimbursement deduction reduces the entity income a PTET election is computed on — sequence the two rather than stacking them.
Missouri: conforms through RSMo §143.121; a Missouri pass-through electing the SALT Parity Act PTET (RSMo §143.436) computes that tax after this deduction.
reviewChecklist: Workforce survey supports the ICHRA over group coverage or a QSEHRA, including premium-tax-credit displacement math.
Class design checked line-by-line against Reg. §54.9802-4, with minimum class sizes verified.
90-day notice delivered and documented; substantiation workflow live with the administrator.
Affordability computation on file where the client is an applicable large employer.
Owner participation limited to those the exclusion actually covers.

client.teaser: Set a fixed health budget and let each employee pick coverage that fits their life.
client.headline: Health benefits with a budget you control — no group plan needed
plainEnglish: Group health insurance means one plan for everyone and premium hikes every year. There is another way. Your business gives each employee a set monthly allowance, tax-free, to buy the health plan they choose on the individual market.
Every dollar is deductible to the business. You set the budget, so there are no renewal surprises. Employees keep coverage that belongs to them, not to the job.

You can set different allowance amounts for different groups — full-time and part-time, for example — as long as everyone in a group is treated the same. Any size of business can use it, and there is no cap on the allowance.
client.analogy: Instead of buying one bus everyone must ride, you hand out travel allowances and let each person pick the ride that gets them home.
benefits: Deductible to the business, tax-free to employees
A fixed budget you set — no more renewal shock
Works at any company size, with no dollar cap
Employees keep coverage they chose themselves
steps: WE compare the ICHRA against your current coverage and your team's facts.
WE design the classes, allowances, plan documents, and required notices.
YOU collect proof of coverage through the administrator and pay reimbursements monthly.
WE revisit the allowances each year as premiums move.
clientCommitments: Reimburse only employees with current proof of their own coverage
Deliver the annual employee notice on schedule
Tell us before changing who gets which benefit level

annualMaintenance: Annual allowance reset against individual-market premium changes
Affordability re-test where the employer mandate applies

Affordability analysis for applicable large employers
